1-2: Trees or posts in a row: one gap fewer than the trees, and the length of the row from the gap between two.
Cutting a ribbon or sawing a log: one cut fewer than the pieces, and the time all the cuts take.
Pages read from one page to another, both ends counted.
Going up a house: one flight fewer than the floor reached, and the steps of all the flights.
Children standing between two others in a line: how many there are, from the places of the two.
Bushes along the sides of a square, one in every corner: the corners counted once.
A child counted from the front and from the back of a queue: how many are in it.
A frog jumping along a row of stones, skipping one stone each time: the jumps to the last.
Beads on a closed necklace: as many gaps as beads.
A clock striking: the time from the first stroke to the last counted in gaps.
3-4: Trees along a road a given distance apart: the length of the row, or the number of trees.
A log cut into pieces of a given length: the cuts, and the time they take.
Whole numbers from one number to another, both ends counted.
A building's floors and flights: the steps from one floor to another.
A closed ring of beads or posts: as many gaps as objects.
A bell ringing at equal spaces: the time for more rings from the time for a few.
A pupil counted from the left and from the right: the length of the row.
Square tables pushed together in a row, one seat to a side: how many people can sit around them.
A train of carriages with links between them, and the length of the whole train.
Pages numbered on both sides of the sheets: how many sheets a run of pages takes.
5-6: A cake or a sheet cut along lines in two directions: the pieces from the cuts.
Trees planted on a rectangular grid of rows, with a tree at every corner.
Children in a circle, numbered in turn: who stands opposite whom.
Tearing a sheet of stamps into single stamps: each tear splits one piece into two.
Strips around the panes of a window: shared sides counted once.
Lamps along a closed path put up again at a new spacing: which places keep a lamp.
Posts round a square or rectangular field, with a post at each corner.
Two paths touching at one point, like a figure eight, and posts along both.
Laps of a running track and the markers passed between two points.
A rope folded several times and cut through once: how many pieces fall apart.
